# A Constellation of Gratitude {.unnumbered}

No book is written in isolation. Behind these pages stands a lifetime of encounters, quiet debts, and the unwavering grace of those who shaped both the writer and the practitioner.

To my parents, I owe the very architecture of my mind. My father, Binod Ghimire, an author in his own right, and my mother, Professor Beena Poudyal, cultivated a home where books were not decorative objects, but living companions and wise elders. Childhood birthdays were never marked by ephemeral toys; they were marked by volumes chosen with care by my mother. They built the quiet foundation upon which my curiosity rests. While the discipline of publishing runs in our lineage, this work carries a distinct devotion—a seed planted long ago in a house suffused with inquiry and ink.

To my beloved daughter, Aashvi: your arrival dismantled and reordered my world. You became the silent catalyst that turned my gaze toward the esoteric arts, setting me on a quest for meaning that eventually took form in these chapters. You gave me my calling, my patience, and an enduring wonder for life. Alongside you, I honor Ms. Anita Pandit, whose presence completed the circle of our family.

To my revered teacher, Guru Bal Krishna Acharya: my deepest pranam. In bringing sacred Vedic wisdom into modern, accessible forums without diluting its rigor, you unlocked the gate for seekers like me. Immersing myself in classical pillars such as the *Laghu Jatakam* and *Laghu Parashari* under your guidance anchored my intuition in disciplined tradition. Without your discernment, the foundations of my practice would not stand.

To my sister, Barsha Ghimire: your faith in me has been an unshakable compass. Long before this manuscript existed, your playful challenge—"Remember to mention my name when you succeed"—was our quiet pact. You did not write these words, but your confidence is woven into the courage required to finish them.

To my friend Prem Regmi: you were the first to urge me past hesitation and onto this path. In the fragile beginning, when doubt ran high, you entrusted me with hundreds of charts, offering the crucible through which theoretical knowledge became living experience. More crucially, you imparted an early, sobering lesson: that our words can alter the trajectory of human choices, and that an ethical guide never uses prediction to strip away human agency.

Finally, to the reader holding this volume: you are entering a conversation built upon love, lineage, and hard-won lessons. May the goodwill of those who nurtured this work guide you in service of those who seek your counsel.
